verses.text: Woe to those who go down to Egypt for help, and rely on horses, and trust in chariots because they are many, and in horsemen because they are very strong, but they don’t look to the Holy One of Israel, and they don’t seek Yahweh!
Yet he also is wise, and will bring disaster, and will not call back his words, but will arise against the house of the evildoers, and against the help of those who work iniquity.

Now the Egyptians are men, and not God; and their horses flesh, and not spirit. When Yahweh stretches out his hand, both he who helps shall stumble, and he who is helped shall fall, and they all shall be consumed together.

For Yahweh says to me, “As the lion and the young lion growling over his prey, if a multitude of shepherds is called together against him, will not be dismayed at their voice, nor abase himself for their noise, so Yahweh of Armies will come down to fight on Mount Zion and on its heights.
As birds hovering, so Yahweh of Armies will protect Jerusalem. He will protect and deliver it. He will pass over and preserve it.”
Return to him from whom you have deeply revolted, children of Israel.
For in that day everyone shall cast away his idols of silver and his idols of gold — sin which your own hands have made for you.
“The Assyrian will fall by the sword, not of man; and the sword, not of mankind, shall devour him. He will flee from the sword, and his young men will become subject to forced labor.
His rock will pass away by reason of terror, and his princes will be afraid of the banner,” says Yahweh, whose fire is in Zion, and his furnace in Jerusalem.

footnotes.content: The heart of temptation: looking everywhere but to the One who can actually help. How many times have I done this—reached for what seemed strong and visible, when all along the Holy One was waiting to be sought. Horses and chariots are so reassuring; trusting an invisible God is the harder road.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: God's wisdom isn't soft—it brings disaster to those who choose the path of evildoing. When we see catastrophe, we should ask not 'Why is God cruel?' but 'What am I trusting in that He has to tear down?' His word stands; He doesn't take back His warnings out of sentiment.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The plainest truth: Egyptians are men, horses are flesh. No spirit, no god-life. When the Holy One stretches out His hand, all that muscle and strategy falls like grain before a reaper. I've learned in my own small troubles that the difference between trust in flesh and trust in God is the difference between sinking sand and bedrock.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Listen to this image: a lion with its prey, unmoved by shepherds shouting. That's the Lord for Zion—a defender who cannot be intimidated or distracted from His people. All the noise and threat in the world doesn't shake Him. He will come down; we don't need to run.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Birds hovering over their nest—alert, sheltering, always present. That's the picture of God over Jerusalem, over us. Protect, deliver, pass over like on Passover night, preserve. Not distant, not occasional. Hovering means He hasn't left the post.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Return. Such a gentle word for such a grave thing—we've deeply revolted. But it's the only word needed: come back. He doesn't say 'crawl back, begging,' just return. As if He's been at the door waiting, and He only asks us to turn around and walk toward Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Silver and gold idols cast away—sin made with our own hands. How hard it is to unmake what we've made sacred. But that day is coming when those lovely lies will just—finally—fall away. What we trust in now instead of God, we will see for what it is.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Assyrian—great power, feared by nations—will fall not by human sword but by the sword of the Lord. Notice: not destroyed by another army, but by judgment itself. Young men dragged away. The mightiest empire brought low not by cleverness but by the Word of God.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: His rock will pass away in terror—and reading this now, we hear an echo of all the strong towers that have crumbled, all the confidence that evaporated, all the princes who found their banners no defense. The furnace in Jerusalem burns still. God hasn't moved from His throne.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
